sentences.text:
Author: T. Vinod Kumar Bench: T. Vinod Kumar  THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE T. VINOD KUMAR  WRIT PETITION No.32856 of 2014 ORDER:
None appears for the petitioners.
Heard learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1 to 3, and perused the record.

2. The case of the petitioners as set out in the affidavit filed in support of the Writ Petition in brief is that aggrieved by the Award dated 31-12-1998 with regard to determination of compensation payable under the Act, the petitioners have approached the respondent No.3 authority and submitted application under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act') on 19- 02-1999 seeking reference; and that in spite of the petitioners submitting the aforesaid application seeking reference under Section 18 of the Act, the same has not been referred by the respondent No.3 authority which action it is claimed as illegal, arbitrary and contrary to the provisions of the Act.

3. Written instructions as placed on record by respondents indicate that the aforesaid application submitted by the petitioners has not been referred to the Civil Court for redetermination of market value due to non-availability of records with the respondent No.3 as the said records were seized by the Anti Corruption Bureau authorities on 08-02-1999 in connection with a trap on one of the employees of the respondent-Office.
4. I have noted the contentions of the petitioners and the submissions made on behalf of the respondents.

5. Admittedly, the petitioners aggrieved by the Award dated 31-12-1998 passed by the respondent No.3 had filed an application under Section 18 of the Act seeking reference to the Civil Court for determination of market value of the land and structures of the petitioners acquired by the respondent authorities, and the said application has not been referred to the Civil Court for determining the market value as provided under the Act.

6. Though, the respondent authorities have claimed that the aforesaid records have been seized by the Anti Corruption Bureau authorities, the said reason by itself cannot take away the right of the petitioners seeking reference under the Act.

9. As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending if any shall stand closed.
